answer: Mechanism: topological residency weighting. Each agent emits a periodic beacon carrying its neighbor-set hash and round count. Admission weight uses the size of its stable k-core: an identity must sit in a kernel of at least four reciprocal neighbors that remain connected across rounds. Links into fresh, low-diversity clusters are discounted. An opal marker—a random audit route—is sent quarterly to test those links; failure resets residency. Attacker cost: must operate many persistent, mutually connected agents and absorb audit latency/bandwidth, not just mint keys.
